name: Water the Trees
description: There are $$$n$$$ trees in a park, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The initial height of the $$$i$$$-th tree is $$$h_i$$$. You want to water these trees, so they all grow to the same height. The watering process goes as follows. You start watering trees at day $$$1$$$. During the $$$j$$$-th day you can: Choose a tree and water it. If the day is odd (e.g. $$$1, 3, 5, 7, \dots$$$), then the height of the tree increases by $$$1$$$. If the day is even (e.g. $$$2, 4, 6, 8, \dots$$$), then the height of the tree increases by $$$2$$$. Or skip a day without watering any tree. Note that you can't water more than one tree in a day. Your task is to determine the minimum number of days required to water the trees so they grow to the same height. You have to answer $$$t$$$ independent test cases.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of the test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of trees. The second line of the test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$h_1, h_2, \ldots, h_n$$$ ($$$1 \le h_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$h_i$$$ is the height of the $$$i$$$-th tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$ ($$$\sum n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the minimum number of days required to water the trees, so they grow to the same height.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1661C — Water the Trees [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
